title: Zipper at the Closure
hook: The right dies. Both lanes still run.
scene: Daylight rain, morning, I-90 east. A work zone ate the right in a half mile. Both lanes still run. Cones pinch toward the closure paint. The early-move habit wants the left now, to be polite, to be first. The zipper wants both lanes used until the teeth, then one-for-one. This is not a courtesy slide and it is not two lanes in one sweep. The handheld clicks once — Yuna, short, not a lecture.
decision: The right lane ends ahead. When do you zipper?

options.text: Use the right until the closure paint, then take turns with the left
options.result: You use the lane until it ends. At the teeth you take one, give one. The stack is shorter than the polite line that started a mile early. She clicks once and stays quiet.

options.text: Move left now so you are not the person who cuts at the end
options.result: You join the polite line. The right stays empty and angry. Someone late uses it and you resent them for doing the zipper. Early courtesy built the longer stack.

options.text: Straddle both lanes until the last cone so nobody can beat you
options.result: You occupy two lanes in a highway work zone. Nobody zippers. You are the blockage the cones were trying to prevent.

options.text: Brake in the right and wave the left through so they go first
options.result: You plant the Menace to look kind. The right stack lights. Take-turns is one-for-one at the teeth, not a courtesy stop in a live lane.

debrief: Use both lanes until the closure, then take turns. The zipper is take-turns, not an early courtesy move.

source.psdp_skill: Skill eleven: highway driving – part two
source.teaching_target: NEW. Cite 5.3 Merging (Zipper merging). Highway work-zone / lane-closure take-turns. Not courtesy move-over. Not V-010 one-lane-at-a-time.
source.stat_cited: DOL p.160–161: zipper merging — use both lanes until the designated merge, then alternate.
